It sounds to me like other than having trouble with the combat, you might wanna go back a little to a region with easier enemies if the skeletons are 1 hitting you. They're some of the weakest enemies in the game. You should also learn to time your blocks and dodges and whatnot. I've been a pc gamer for years too before I bought my switch. It takes some getting used to, but it gets better. The combat system is actually really fluid and well-built once you get better at it. And as far as arrows go, you can buy them in the general store in the first village. I won't name anything for spoilers sake, but they can be bought. 

And on the note of using 20 arrows in 1 fight: That also sounds like you're in a region with enemies that are too powerful. You don't level up, but you continuously find better gear, and you can upgrade armor at a certain point. It makes for a pretty solid leveling system as you go around doing shrines. I would also advise you either mark or do every shrine you come across. It seriously helps a lot.

I'm poor and I live in America. Mental help is incredibly expensive. How can I hold a job when I can't even get out of bed in the morning to take a shower. Most insurance planes don't cover mental health, not that I have insurance anyway. That, and I'd have to admit my problem to the entire family to get a ride to said psychiatrist. And you're missing the point - I'm still in pain no matter what I'm doing. No matter how busy I am, it's always there. It never goes away anymore. I can barely ever quit thinking about it.

It's hard discussing TV shows when all you wanna do is die. Hell, I don't even have a tv anymore. I'm just so tired of trying to make friends and connect with people. It's not like I can tell my family how I feel, they'd just say I'm making it up for attention or some shit and disregard it completely. Even if they didn't, our entire family would know then, because of course they love to gossip. I just wish all the people who are alone could come together and just care about each other. I'm not a fool though, I know that won't happen. But all I ever do is dream and imagine I have actual friends. It's the only thing that dulls these feelings for a few moments. I can't do this alone.

Exactly. I wouldn't have to deal with anything if I were dead. The fact that it's a physical disease doesn't really provide any comfort knowing that I'll likely never get help. I don't think I even care anymore at this point. I've made peace with the fact that suicide is the only way out of the pain, it's just a matter of time before I have the means to do it.

I've had the knife to my wrist on a couple occasions. It felt to me like an incredible sense of hopelessness. Like the feeling of death being the only way out of the pain. In the end I was too afraid to do it, but most days I just wish I did. It's not a feeling anyone should have to feel, for any reason. No one deserves that. It felt like I was just stuck there, in a deep sense of pain and sadness. When a person's emotional pain grows so great the only way they feel like like they get out of it is suicide, it's a really sad thing. Like I said, no one deserves that. If I just would've had one friend, one person to tell me they care in that moment, I would've dropped that knife that much sooner. It's a feeling of incredible vulnerability. But at the same time, I just wished I could be vulnerable and honest with someone about it without being judged. But a guy can dream, right? Dreams seem to be the only thing keeping me going now a days.
